## TL;DR

The phone Work page mounted **both** layouts because the desktop `v-else` was chained to `MobileTaskDetail`, not to the narrow layout. On a phone with no task open, `mobileTaskSelected` is false, so the detail did not render and the `v-else` desktop board rendered *in addition to* the always-mounted mobile queue. The board painted over the lower half of the queue, which is exactly what the v0.5.83 screenshots show. I reproduced it at 360, 390 and 412 px with a mounted `WorkView` under a narrow `matchMedia`, fixed the conditional structure, kept the integration bar outside the desktop-only branch, made the queue's end clearance rely on the shared page inset, and added a review-task **Move to done** action gated on the same landing pre-checks the desktop drawer uses. A parameterized phone-width test now fails if both queues ever render again, and a WebKit geometry test covers the queue's bottom clearance.

## Work and rationale

**The layout bug.** `WorkView` rendered `<MobileWorkQueue v-if="isNarrow">`, then `<MobileTaskDetail v-if="mobileTaskSelected">`, then `<div v-else class="work-page">`. In Vue, `v-else` binds to the *immediately preceding* `v-if`/`v-else-if` element — here the detail component. So the desktop branch's condition was "a mobile task is not selected", which is true whenever the phone is showing the queue. The mobile queue and the desktop board therefore rendered together, and the desktop board's columns (plus its fixed pipeline bar) covered the mobile cards. The mobile header count and the board's counts disagreed for the same reason: two independent filters were visible at once.

The fix wraps the narrow composition in its own `<template v-if="isNarrow">` and leaves the desktop `v-else` chained to that template. The queue stays mounted with `v-show` while the detail is open so its filter/sort state survives Back, and the detail still uses `v-if`. I chose unmounting over `display:none` for the desktop branch: the acceptance criteria allow either, and unmounting avoids building the board columns, its keyboard-nav task list and its parked lists on a phone where they can never be seen.

**The integration bar.** It lived inside `.work-page`, so hiding the desktop branch would also have removed the phone's pipeline status. It is ambient Work UI, not part of the board, so I hoisted `<IntegrationStatusBar>` to the view root. Its existing `@media (max-width: 719.98px)` rules already float it above the tab bar; the queue is a direct child of `.main`, so it inherits `padding-bottom: var(--page-bottom-inset)` on its own scroller. The queue also had a 120 px bottom spacer on top of that inset, which left roughly a third of a phone screen blank at the end of the list; I reduced it to 16 px now that the inset is demonstrably doing the work.

**The status filter and count.** `MobileWorkQueue` already filtered `repo.tasks` (excluding archived/held) and rendered the same array it counted, so once the board was gone the header count and list agreed by construction. I left the filter local rather than syncing it to `?status=`: the desktop filter is URL-backed because it is a board deep-link, while the phone's compact filter is a session control, and adding router writes would churn history on every select. The visible list, the count and the sort all read one computed array.

**Task detail actions.** The detail already had Start work, Pause work and Move to ready with 46 px targets. The one missing primary action for a review task was **Move to done**, which the task spec names explicitly. I added it behind `repo.landableFor(id).landable`, the same read-only landing pre-checks the drawer uses, so a phone tap cannot bypass merge readiness. While the checks load the button is disabled with "Checking merge readiness…"; a failing check is shown by label and detail; if the server cannot answer, the action stays disabled and says the readiness could not be checked. On success the detail returns to the queue, closes the panel, expands the integration bar and toasts that close-out started. Dirty-checkout and handoff-conflict errors surface inline, the same messages the store already produces. I also raised the queue's status, sort and reset controls from 40 px to 44 px so the filter row meets the touch-target floor.

## Approaches tried

- **`display:none` on `.work-page` below 720 px** — would have been a one-line CSS fix and the criterion allows it, but it still mounts the whole board (columns, keyboard list, parked lists) on every phone render. The `v-if` restructure is the same size and cheaper.
- **Syncing the mobile status filter to `?status=`** — rejected as extra router churn; the requirement is that the visible list and count agree, which the single computed array guarantees.
- **A full review surface on mobile** (land-anyway, dirty-checkout commit dialog, review report) — out of scope for this p0 layout bug and owned by the sibling mobile Work task (#0303). I added only the close-out action that can be safely gated by existing read-only checks.
- **Leaving the 120 px spacer** — safe but produced a large dead tail; the WebKit geometry test showed the inset alone clears the fixed controls, so I trimmed it.

## Challenges and blockers

- **No real device or live server was available in this run.** I could not open a v0.5.87 build on Nick's phone. Reproduction is from a mounted `WorkView` at 360/390/412 px with a narrow `matchMedia` stub: before the fix that test found both `[data-testid="mobile-work-queue"]` and `.work-page` in the DOM at all three widths, which is the same double mount the screenshots show. The HEAD code had the identical `v-else` chain, so this is not a bee-only v0.5.83 problem; the screenshots came from the older build, but the bug is in main.
- **Vitest hangs under Node 26 in this environment** when the repo's `globalSetup` (process-reap) is enabled; the same config runs normally under Bun. I ran the focused suites with `bun node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts …`, which matches the runtime `repoos check` uses. This was an environment/runtime difference, not a test failure.
- The managed preview is the human's to request; I did not request one or run a server.

## Key learnings

- `v-else` is a sibling-binding, not a group-binding. Chaining it across a conditional detail view silently made "no task selected" mean "render the desktop board".
- A layout regression test should mount the real view at the reported widths and assert which composition exists; asserting only `isNarrow === true` would have missed this entirely.
- Ambient fixed UI (the pipeline bar) should sit outside viewport-conditional branches so hiding a layout does not hide status.
- The shared `--page-bottom-inset` on the routed scroller is the right place for tab-bar/bar clearance; a second hand-tuned spacer only creates a dead tail.
